profile.tagline: Professor and researcher in electronics engineering, working on deep learning for medical images and biomedical signals, chaos-based cryptography and embedded systems.
profile.summary: Everardo Inzunza-González is a full-time Professor and Researcher (Titular C) at the Faculty of Engineering, Architecture and Design of the Universidad Autónoma de Baja California (UABC) in Ensenada, Mexico, where he has worked since February 2000. He received his B.Sc. in Electronics Engineering from the Instituto Tecnológico de Culiacán, his M.Sc. in Electronics and Telecommunications from CICESE, and his Ph.D. in Electrical Sciences from UABC in 2013, with honorable mention. His recent work applies machine learning and deep learning to medical images and to biomedical signals such as EEG, ECG and heart sounds. He also keeps a line of research on chaos-based cryptography implemented on embedded systems, FPGAs and edge devices. He is a Level 2 member of Mexico's National System of Researchers (SNII, 2025–2029), has held the PRODEP Desirable Profile recognition since 2004, and leads the consolidated research group UABC-CA-238. He is part of the core faculty of the Master's and Doctoral Program in Science and Engineering (MyDCI) and has served as guest editor of special issues in MDPI and Elsevier journals.
